chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from al-Nawfali, from al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) said: 'There is no problem with a man taking dirhams in Mecca and writing for them bills of exchange (safatij) to be paid in Kufa.'
ai.seo_question: What is the Islamic ruling on using bills of exchange for money transfer?
ai.summary: This hadith from Al-Kafi establishes the permissibility of the *sufaja* (bill of exchange), demonstrating an early Islamic financial instrument that allowed merchants to transfer wealth securely between Mecca and Kufa without carrying heavy coinage. It highlights the practical economic needs of the Shia community and the Imam's approval of commercial innovations that facilitated trade and reduced the risk of theft during transit. This ruling underscores the flexibility of Islamic jurisprudence in accommodating evolving economic practices while maintaining the integrity of monetary transactions.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Al Nowfaly, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘Amir Al-Momineen<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘There is no problem with the man taking the Dirhams in Makkah and writes for them a bill of exchange that he would give it in Al-Kufa’.
en.sarwar: 2. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from al-Nawfaliy from al-Sakuniy who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said that
’Amir al-Mu’minin has said, ‘It is not unlawful if a man takes dirhams in Makkah and writes for them (his people) notes to pay them in al-Kufah.’”
